key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation plus ANN models can accurately predict weld temperature, axial force, and defect formation in HDPE friction stir welding, enabling fast process-window optimization.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical guidance for selecting rotational speed, travel speed, and preheating to improve weld quality and reduce wormhole defects in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of FSW under varying rotation speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental data to predict temporal temperature and axial-force responses
Validation against experiments and use of the combined framework to map defect-free vs defective operating windows
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental thermal, mechanical, and void-formation behavior well.
watch_item: The process maps are specific to the tested HDPE setup and parameter range, so transfer to other tool geometries, materials, or thicknesses will need revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
